evidence: Internal premises hold: CURRENT-DESIGN.md:14 specifies a durable journaled queue, one writer and Git commits; DESIGN-NOTES.md:150 separates admission from completion, :159 proposes inspectable operation status, and :152 plus CURRENT-DESIGN.md:15-16 make committed intent the reconciliation basis. Full-text search for journal/queue/commit/crash/recovery/replay/idempotency/operation identity across all four reviewed docs found no selected rule that associates a journal operation with its commit, handles dirty checkout state after interruption, or repairs status after commit-before-completion. DESIGN-NOTES.md:68 calls durable operation identity and unknown outcomes unsettled; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:53 explicitly leaves mutation/journal contracts for later design. The external-effect unknown-outcome rule (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:17; DESIGN-NOTES.md:174) does not specify local writer crash recovery. Thus interruption can leave ambiguous local state/status and undermine the stated durable, inspectable, latest-committed-intent workflow. This is an acknowledged but material design gap; it establishes risk, not actual data loss or a claim of implementation readiness.
